cultural.vision_reason: This is a New Kingdom Egyptian limestone trial/sketch piece carved with four relief head studies, including Egyptian figures (a king and a priest), made and used by ancient Egyptian artists at Thebes—directly matching the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: Trial Piece Worked on Both Sides
physical.summary: This carved flake of limestone provides a fascinating glimpse of the ancient artist at work. One side, by far the better, features four studies of heads. At the upper left is an Asiatic. He has a low forehead, a prominent nose, and a long, pointed beard. To his right is a Nubian wearing the short, round headdress and large loop earring that the Egyptians usually identified with this ethnic group. The bottom row presents images from within Egypt. At the left is a stock image of a king. To his right is another Egyptian, whose clean-shaven head immediately identifies him as a priest.

location.made_in_place: Egypt, probably Thebes, New Kingdom (1540–1069 BCE), Dynasty 18, reign of Amenhotep III (1390–1352 BCE)
